summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have, and don't add chip stocks before Micron's results tomorrow morning. Tonight turns on the US inflation figures at 8:30pm, and I expect the main groups to finish close to where they are now.
summary.where_we_are: 8:18pm SGT (8:18am New York). US pre-market is open and the regular session starts at 9:30pm SGT. Singapore closed at 5pm. Tonight: US PCE inflation for August at 8:30pm SGT. Tomorrow: Micron results at about 4:05am SGT, after the US close.
summary.macro_attribution: Oil has moved most since the last US close, up 1.5% to $90.5, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.26% (prices). My read depends on oil only through what tonight's inflation figures do to that yield.
what_happened: Chip stocks are down 0.8% before the US open (prices), and most of that comes from two names: Cerebras (AI inference chips) is down 5.9% and AMD is down 1.0%, while Nvidia and Broadcom are flat. Pre-market trades carry no volume, so the dip is thin until the open confirms it. I found no news explaining Cerebras.
Asia closed mixed: Nikkei +2.5%, Taiwan +1.0% with TSMC +0.8%, Korea -0.5% (prices). In memory, SK Hynix rose 1.1% and Samsung fell 1.1%.
All three Singapore banks fell today: UOB -1.3%, DBS -1.0% on 1.65× usual volume, OCBC -0.5% (prices). I found no bank-specific news.
US futures are nearly flat, S&P -0.1% and Nasdaq -0.3% (prices). The inflation figure is expected to show prices rising faster in August (Bloomberg, 30 Sep, search summary).

per_group.semis: Flat. The dip is mostly Cerebras and AMD, and traders usually hold positions into Micron's results rather than move the whole group the day before. Chip stocks already sit 6.6% above their 20-day average, so there is no case for adding first.
per_group.big_tech: Flat. Meta's -1.3% and Alphabet's +1.0% before the open roughly cancel, nothing company-specific is due, and the inflation figures could push either way.
per_group.sg_banks: Flat at tomorrow's close. Today's 1% fall came with no news I could find, and the US inflation figures and Micron's results both land before Singapore reopens, which gives no clear direction.
per_group.market: Flat. Futures are barely moving, the VIX (the market's fear gauge) is calm at 16, and a hotter inflation figure is already what analysts expect.

change_my_mind: If the 10-year yield closes above 5.30% after the inflation figures, I would expect chips and big tech to fall more than 0.5%, and the flat call is wrong on the downside.
If the 10-year falls back below 5.20%, I would expect chips to recover this morning's dip, and the call should have been up.
If Cerebras's fall spreads to AMD and Nvidia in the first hour on heavy volume, chips lean down.
summary.confidence: The inflation figures come out 12 minutes after this read and decide the day.
summary.cant_know: How hot the August inflation figure is, and whether traders sell chips before Micron's results or buy them.
summary.the_call: Flat, and quietly. I expect the S&P 500 to finish within about half a percent of where it is now. Chips move the most because of Cerebras's fall and the positioning before Micron. The whole market moves the least.
